messages:
Aisha (PM): Heads up — Liam from sales just forwarded a Kora Health escalation. They saw p95 latency jump ~2x on their dedicated pool after last week's runtime deploy. Sales wants an ETA to avoid contract penalties. Can we triage and decide whether this becomes a product backlog item or support-level mitigation?

Liam (Sales): Copy of customer note: "Since Tue 23:00 UTC, we saw tail latency spike for chat flows (longer contexts). Throughput stayed stable but p95 went from ~150ms -> ~320ms. This affects SLAs for our live ops." They asked for a short-term workaround + timeline.

Maya (Support): Repro steps from their session: lots of 1k+ token requests, model = llm-x-large-v1, region = eu-west1, dedicated pool id dp-77. I pulled logs — lots of KV cache misses during the spike, and batching dropped to single-request batches around the same time.

Maya (Support): snippet from logs:
```
[2025-11-04T22:58:12Z] pool=dp-77 req_id=abc123 seq_len=1024 cache_hit=false batch_size=1 p95=338ms
[2025-11-04T22:58:43Z] pool=dp-77 req_id=def456 seq_len=1102 cache_hit=false batch_size=1 p95=355ms
```

Diego (Eng-runtime): Thanks — useful signals. Two quick asks: (1) Ivy, can you attach the trace for those request ids? Need to see kernel times vs queuing. (2) Sam, any routing changes or autoscale events in that window?

Ivy (Eng-oncall): Trace links: https://telemetry.redwood/trace/abc123 (internal). Looking at spans — token generation time per-token is normal, but there's a consistent ~120-180ms stall before generation starts. Queue depth was low, CPU/GPU utilization normal. :thinking:

Sam (Eng-platform): No routing rules changed. There was a small autoscale event ~22:57 where we spun up one extra worker for dp-77, but it completed ~90s before the first spike sample. No region failover. I suspect cache warming + batch sizing regression.

Alex (SRE): Quick mitigation option: Enable short-term routing fallback to smaller model variant (llm-x-medium) for dp-77 during peak windows and temporarily increase burst capacity for dp-77 to reduce single-request serialization. Can do config flip from console.

Diego (Eng-runtime): Proposed triage path:
- Short-term (support ops, immediate): route Kora to fallback variant + bump burst cap. Ownership: Sam/Alex can do config flips.
- Mid-term (prod backlog, 2-4 weeks): implement automatic cache prewarm for long-context sessions and tweak batching thresholds to avoid single-request batches for high-seq-length flows. Ownership: eng-runtime + eng-platform.
- Long-term (Q1): runtime KV cache refactor + perf regressions test in canary pipeline.

Aisha (PM): Thanks. For backlog prioritization I need acceptance criteria and customer impact quant: target p95 <= 200ms or back to baseline, reproducible test-case, and a minimal rollback plan. Diego, can you put a short spec in the backlog ticket with scope + risks? If we go for mid-term fix, we want a small canary and an ops rollback knob.

Diego (Eng-runtime): Will do. Draft spec will include: data-driven thresholds for batching, metric alarms (p95, cache_miss_rate), and canary rollout steps. ETA for draft: EOD tomorrow.

Maya (Support): Customer asks for ETA by EOD today — sales escalation. Can we confirm the immediate mitigation window (routing flip + burst bump) and I’ll coordinate the customer-facing note?

Sam (Eng-platform): I can flip routing to fallback and bump burst cap now. Will monitor p95 for 30 minutes and report.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued by Sam for dp-77 routing flip -> approved by Alex, starting at 1767345640.

Ivy (Eng-oncall): After flip at 1767345640, initial numbers: p95 dropped from ~340ms -> ~190ms within 3 minutes. Cache_miss_rate reduced by ~40%. Monitoring link: https://telemetry.redwood/alerts/dp-77

Aisha (PM): Great outcome. Next steps: Diego files the backlog ticket with spec + acceptance criteria, Sam writes runbook steps for temporary routing flip, Maya sends customer update with short-term mitigation and timeline for full fix. Marking owner Diego and target delivery (mid-term fix) in 3 weeks.

Liam (Sales): Will craft the customer message and share before EOD. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
